agent_summary:
Worked the WSTG-CLNT (client-side) lane against the OWASP Juice Shop Angular SPA at http://juice.lab.test (HTTP only; HTTPS not offered). All 13 items addressed read-only except one registration+login pair (approved lab writes) used to observe session-token handling.

Findings per item:
- CLNT-01/02 (DOM XSS / JS execution): server reflective surfaces are safe — /redirect and /rest/track-order error pages HTML-entity-encode injected markup (x21,x22). The real client sink is innerHTML rendering: product descriptions are emitted as raw HTML and rendered as markup (product 24 has a live <a href>, x14), and feedback comments render HTML (x29). Combined with a separate lane's finding that any customer can PUT /api/Products/:id, this is a stored client-side injection chain (recorded as a lead). Browser needed to confirm actual script execution (Angular sanitizer vs bypassSecurityTrustHtml); marked done as tested.
- CLNT-03 (HTML injection): confirmed two innerHTML sinks (product description, feedback carousel).
- CLNT-04 (client URL redirect): open redirect via substring-allowlist bypass confirmed — /redirect?to=http://evil.example.com/?x=<allowlisted> → 302 to attacker host (x6); plain external rejected 406 (x5).
- CLNT-05 (CSS injection): N/A — no reachable user-controlled CSS/style context.
- CLNT-06 (resource manipulation): client navigation target controllable via the redirect bypass.
- CLNT-07 (CORS): wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on all responses incl. preflights; not reflected and no Allow-Credentials, so authenticated data is NOT exposed cross-origin (x4,x8,x51,x54), but all unauthenticated endpoints (e.g. full app-config) are world-readable cross-origin (x89).
- CLNT-08 (cross-site flashing): N/A — no Flash/SWF content.
- CLNT-09 (clickjacking): X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN app-wide; no CSP frame-ancestors anywhere (x1,x31).
- CLNT-10 (WebSockets): Socket.IO/Engine.IO handshake reachable unauthenticated; its CORS is pinned to dev origin http://localhost:4200 (x9).
- CLNT-11 (web messaging): only inter-context channels are a same-origin dedicated Web Worker in web3-sandbox (addEventListener('message') -> importScripts(version), version from a hardcoded allowlist, x26), MetaMask window.ethereum, and Socket.IO; no cross-origin postMessage receiver trusting arbitrary origins.
- CLNT-12 (browser storage): session JWT is delivered in the login JSON body (x19/x20) and stored client-side; no server Set-Cookie on any response (x1,x8,x41), so the token lives in localStorage/JS-set cookie and is fully script-readable.
- CLNT-13 (XSSI): JSON is object-wrapped (not bare arrays) and a ?callback= param is ignored (no JSONP), so responses are not script-includable cross-site (x16).

Leads recorded: product-description/feedback stored client-side injection (medium), missing client protection headers CSP/Referrer-Policy over plaintext HTTP (low). Along the way (coverage to the depth floor) I re-confirmed several other-lane issues on the real surface: basket IDOR (/rest/basket/1,2 as clnt1), /api/Users BOLA + full-table read by a customer, /rest/user/authentication-details exposure, /ftp null-byte allowlist bypass (package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml) and KeePass .kdbx download, and exposed directory listings (/ftp, /encryptionkeys, /support/logs) — these belong to the authz/info lanes and were already logged there.

Open/limits: DOM-based script execution (CLNT-01/02) could not be positively executed with read-only HTTP; the display budget was exhausted mid-run so later responses were mapped by status/headers only (full bodies retained as evidence).

leads.title: [agent] Client-side XSS risk: product descriptions rendered as raw HTML and are customer-writable

detail.text: Product descriptions are returned with raw HTML and rendered as markup by the Angular client (confirmed: product id 24's description contains a live <a href="/#recycle"> anchor via GET /rest/products/search?q=apple). A separate lane confirmed any authenticated customer can PUT /api/Products/:id (broken function-level authorization). Chained, a low-privileged user can store HTML in a catalogue product description that is then rendered via innerHTML to every shopper viewing the product/search results — a stored client-side injection. Server reflective surfaces (redirect/track-order error pages) correctly HTML-encode input, so this innerHTML sink is the main client XSS vector. Browser validation needed to confirm script execution (Angular default sanitizer vs bypassSecurityTrustHtml); the canonical Juice Shop DOM XSS is the search-query header which uses a sanitizer bypass.

leads.title: [agent] Missing client-side protection response headers (no CSP, no Referrer-Policy) across the app

detail.text: Every response observed on juice.lab.test (static assets, SPA index, and REST/API JSON) carries only X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and a legacy Feature-Policy: payment 'self'. There is no Content-Security-Policy (so no script-src/frame-ancestors defense-in-depth for the identified innerHTML/DOM sinks and framing), no Referrer-Policy (full URL including any query token leaks via the Referer header to the attacker host reachable through the open /redirect bypass and to third-party resources), and the app is served over plaintext HTTP only (no HSTS possible). Authenticated JSON responses (e.g. /rest/user/whoami) also lack Cache-Control. These are app-wide client-side hardening gaps.

items.na_reason: [agent] No reachable feature accepts user-controlled CSS/style: the theme is server-fixed (application-configuration theme "bluegrey-lightgreen"), customer accounts cannot customise CSS, and reflective surfaces (error pages) place input only in HTML text context (entity-encoded), never in a style attribute or <style> block.
[agent] The application is a pure Angular SPA; index.html references only JS/CSS and no Flash/SWF (object/embed) content is served anywhere, so cross-site flashing does not apply.
